thread:
Mira Patel: heads up — hosted-usw2 headroom dashboard just flickered. p95 queue climbed to 3.2s and some pools show lots of small free slots but no pod fits (slot fragmentation). ops-bot posted alert.
ops-bot: ALERT hosted-usw2: pool_util=0.93 headroom=7% small_free_slots=112 fragmentation_index=0.67
Kai Huang: saw that. requests are spiky from a new internal loadtest. looks like many requests are single-token and we have lots of 2-4 slot fragments.
Samir Desai: can we force packing for a short window? bin-packing would reduce fragmentation but risk higher p95 for batched traffic.
Mira Patel: @Kai can you share the exact loadtest job id? want to see request shape. also @SRE-Oncall check if autoscaler reacted.
Kai Huang: job id: loadtest/2026-03-20-usw2-a12. sample qps: 1200 with 78% single-token requests. here's a quick kusto query I used:
```
select avg(token_count) as avg_tokens, percentile(token_count, 95) as p95_tokens
from requests
where job_id = 'loadtest/2026-03-20-usw2-a12' and region='usw2'
```
Leo Turner: autoscaler scaled +10 nodes but those nodes are coming up with 1-slot fragments due to image packing. we need node-level prewarm that coalesces similar instance types.
Eva Gómez: rebalancer is currently conservative — it avoids moving warm KV caches. moving could drop cache hit and spike latency.
Samir Desai: Idea: short-lived aggressive compaction: schedule a rolling compact job that evicts tiny pods and refills with appropriately sized pods, but keep a % of cache-carrying pods pinned.
Mira Patel: risk assessment? what's the expected p95 delta during compaction? and cost impact (extra on-demand minutes)?
SRE-Oncall: rough numbers from previous compaction run in euw1: transient p95 +0.8s for ~6 minutes, CPU burn ~0.4 node-min per pool. had to abort once due to a concurrent deploy.
Kai Huang: alternative — enable request-level spill-to-dedicated for customers flagged as non-critical in config. that reduces hosted pressure but increases billing complexity.
Eva Gómez: we can also tweak the admission controller fallback window to be more tolerant for single-token requests; let them inline instead of waiting for a batch slot.
Leo Turner: quick mitigation I can push: change packing policy to prefer 1x8-slot pods over many 1x1 pods for the next 10m. will require node cordon/drain of a few underutilized nodes.
Mira Patel: do it if you think it's safe. coordinate with SRE-Oncall before drain. also add a short dashboard annotation so we can correlate.
SRE-Oncall: starting coordination. @Leo please post exact nodes you'll drain. will hold traffic re-routes until drain starts.
Leo Turner: nodes: g4-usw2-n[112-114]. draining now (will take ~90s each). switching packing policy for 10m.
ops-bot: NOTICE packing_policy changed: prefer_large_pods=true duration=10m by Leo Turner
Kai Huang: after first node drain p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 2.1s, queue length down 18%. KV hit unchanged so far.
Samir Desai: good sign. keep an eye on tail errors — if we see OOMKill spike we abort.
Eva Gómez: monitoring: no cache-evictions, no OOM. qps steady but less queuing.
Mira Patel: next steps: 1) keep packing policy for 10m then revert and analyze. 2) create a small runbook for fragmentation compaction. 3) follow-up task to improve scheduler heuristics.
Kai Huang: logging the runbook notes in #eng-infra-runbooks. short-term billing: ~0.6 node-min extra, should be fine.
SRE-Oncall: marking thread resolved for now. reopen if p95 > 2.5s in next 15m.
Mira Patel: thanks team. great run. :thumbsup:
